advisory.issue: Deeply nested brace patterns can trigger stack exhaustion in recursive AST walkers.

dependencyPath.production: NONE. pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server list --prod --depth Infinity --parseable resolves httpxy@0.5.5 and no http-proxy-middleware, micromatch, or braces.
dependencyPath.productionReplacement: @workspace/api-server dependencies -> httpxy@0.5.5; this is the proxy engine previously used internally by http-proxy-middleware.

mitigation.coverage: Depth guards protect the recursive parse/expand paths while retaining ordinary brace expansion.
mitigation.runtimeBundleVerification: API typecheck and production build passed; the six depth-guard tests and three local-target Clerk proxy contract tests passed.

runtimeExposureAssessment.productionUse: The production Clerk proxy uses httpxy@0.5.5 directly and preserves the existing route prefix handling, proxy headers, and response handling. http-proxy-middleware remains only as a development dependency for the existing braces depth-guard regression tests.
runtimeExposureAssessment.assessment: The vulnerable package is not in the API production dependency tree or either emitted API executable bundle. The raw audit finding remains visible and is restricted to the two recorded development-only chains.

releaseImplication: The dependency audit still reports the High advisory against braces@3.0.3; do not suppress it or present the scanners as clean. The only exception is for this exact finding because it is absent from the production API dependency tree and production bundles, with the patched development paths retained under depth-guard tests. Any production path, different critical/high finding, or failed evidence check blocks release.
